question: Will Brazil's STF hold an in-person plenary judgment session on October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Two gates: Oct 1 must be on the October pauta (not yet published; STF portal unreachable), and the session must convene with quorum and take up a case. The court's 2026 rhythm is Wed+Thu weekly (Sept 2-3, 9-10, 16-17, 23-24, 30), and Sept 30 is confirmed as a substantive in-person day, so the election week is not being cleared wholesale — Oct 1 as the Thursday pair is likely scheduled (~85%). The conditional hold rate is the problem: Fachin cancelled four plenary sessions in three weeks (Sept 9, 10, 17, 23) versus three held (Sept 2, 3, 16), he is publicly reported to fear sessions without the six-minister quorum, Toffoli is absent and Nunes Marques impeded, and ministers project migrating work to the virtual plenary, which does not count here. Offsetting: Dino's vista (up to 90 days) and the removal of the Mendonca case park the flashpoints past the election, Sept 16 showed the plenary resuming ordinary tax/civil docket, and the YES bar is low once a session opens. 0.85 x ~0.78.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off credible media reporting about what the STF plenary actually did on Thursday 1 Oct 2026 (Brasilia time) — not off the published pauta, not off virtual-plenary (electronic) judgments, not off Turma, administrative or solemn sessions, and not off a session that only reads a decision or hears oral argument without discussing/voting a case.
EVENT WINDOW: 1 Oct 2026 00:00 -> 23:59 Brasilia, a single calendar day, per the criteria; as of Now (2026-09-21T10:10Z) 0% elapsed, ~10 days ahead. Oct 1 is a Thursday; first-round general elections are Sunday 4 Oct 2026; a possible runoff is 25 Oct.
STATUS QUO: the STF is not in recess (2026 recess per the official calendar runs 20 Dec 2026-6 Jan 2027); Thursday is an ordinary plenary day and the court's 2026 pattern is Wednesday+Thursday sittings each week.
EVIDENCE:
- Sept 2026 pauta as published by Conjur (29 Aug 2026): in-person plenary days 2-3, 9-10, 16-17, 23-24 and 30 September — Wed+Thu every week of the month.
- The October 2026 pauta was not published/indexed as of 21 Sep 2026 (September's was released ~29 Aug). STF's own sites (portal.stf.jus.br, noticias.stf.jus.br) were not retrievable this run (TLS failure / HTTP 403), so Oct 1's presence on the pauta is unverified.
- Fachin cancelled the plenary sessions of Wed 9 Sep and Thu 10 Sep 2026 (Agencia Brasil, O Tempo, 10 Sep) amid the Master-case crisis.
- An extraordinary session was held Tue 15 Sep on whether to investigate Moraes (Pet 16.662); it ended with Flavio Dino's pedido de vista, which he may hold up to 90 days — past both 4 Oct and 25 Oct (Metropoles, 17 Sep; G1, 20 Sep). Tally reported at 4-4 with Fachin's casting vote itself disputed.
- Ordinary sessions resumed Wed 16 Sep, opened ~14:50, with the plenary judging non-crisis matters (ITBI immunity, RE 1.495.108) and no official mention of the dispute (n1n, 16 Sep; TV Brasil).
- Thu 17 Sep: Fachin cancelled that day's extraordinary plenary session after a fresh public clash between Gilmar Mendes and Mendonca, and removed the Mendonca matter (Pet 16.704) from the 23 Sep agenda with no new date (Migalhas, Bahia Noticias, Times Brasil, 17 Sep).
- Remaining September in-person plenary days per court calendar as reported on 18-20 Sep: 24 Sep (block of ICMS fiscal-benefit cases, municipal prosecutor pay) and 30 Sep (blood transfusion against patient's wishes; psychology council rules). The 23 Sep in-person session is off (O Brasilianista, 18 Sep; Noveen).
- O Tempo (16 Sep): 'ja entrou no radar do presidente do STF a possibilidade de que, em muitas das sessoes vindouras, nem haja quorum'; RISTF requires a minimum of six ministers present for a plenary session; a judgment of constitutionality requires eight present (Lei 9.868 art. 22).
- Quorum-relevant absences reported: Dias Toffoli already-planned absence; Nunes Marques declared himself impedido in the Master-case matters; several ministers described upcoming sessions as 'contaminated' and were weighing staying away.
- Ministers project heavier use of the VIRTUAL plenary as the workaround for confrontation-avoidance (O Tempo, 16 Sep). Virtual sessions already scheduled 18-25 Sep and 25 Sep-2 Oct (a virtual session therefore spans 1 Oct, and does not count for this question).
- Still-pending flashpoints that could re-ignite before 1 Oct: Fachin's decisions on suspension of PF director Andrei Rodrigues and on resuming the Master and INSS inquiries; the unresolved question of whether the president-as-relator can cast a tie-break vote (G1, 20 Sep).
- Pre-election context: the crisis is a live campaign topic; reporting frames the Moraes question as likely to cross the election without an answer (Metropoles, 17 Sep). Several ministers had signalled reluctance to have the court act on politically charged matters near the vote. Three STF ministers also sit on the TSE, which is in its most intense phase in the final week before 4 Oct.
BASE RATES:
- Over all scheduled ordinary in-person STF plenary session days outside recess (normal years): the large majority convene and judge at least one case; cancellations are uncommon and usually stem from lack of quorum, mourning, or recess (class: all pauta'd plenary days, long run).
- Over September 2026 specifically (class: pauta'd ordinary plenary days during the Master crisis, 1-23 Sep): held 2, 3, 16 Sep; cancelled 9, 10, 17, 23 Sep — i.e. 3 of 7 decided days held, with 24 and 30 Sep still pending.
- Over sessions held during the crisis (class: crisis-period sessions that did convene): each took up and judged ordinary docket cases (ITBI etc.), i.e. convening has so far implied judging at least one case.
SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: the October 2026 plenary pauta (any outlet); any STF nota a imprensa suspending or confirming sessions for the election week; any explicit rule or past practice statement that the STF suspends in-person plenary sessions in the week before a general election; verified session-by-session records for the equivalent pre-election weeks of 2014/2018/2022 (Informativo 919 covers 8-12 Oct 2018 and Informativo 1070 is dated 7 Oct 2022, but I could not open the documents to confirm which in-person plenary sittings those weeks contained); any prediction market whose contract matches this question's terms (the one similar-titled Polymarket contract is about impeachment of a justice before 2027, a different event, deadline and instrument).
calls.reference_class: Scheduled ordinary in-person STF plenary session days outside recess that actually convene with quorum and judge at least one case

calls.reasoning: Reference class: STF ordinary Wed/Thu in-person plenary session days on the published calendar actually convening with quorum and taking up >=1 case — normally ~0.90. Two discounts apply. (1) Scheduling: I could not verify Oct 1 is on the October pauta; recovered October highlights name only later dates (Oct 8 onward), and Oct 1 sits three days before the Oct 4 first round, a week in which several justices signalled reluctance to have the Court act. (2) Regime: in September 2026 Fachin cancelled at least four plenary sessions (9, 10, 17, 23) amid the Master-case crisis, an unprecedented rate; a deliberate quorum break was reported as a live tactic. Offsetting: the acute trigger is parked (Dino's vista, up to 90 days) and the crisis items are being deferred past the elections, the Court resumed ordinary judging on Sept 16, the October agenda was published normally, and Fachin has an institutional interest in projecting normality on a routine tax/rights docket. Thin, one-sided sourcing on the specific date keeps me near the reference class minus those discounts rather than far from it.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off credible reporting that an IN-PERSON (presencial) STF plenary JUDGMENT session convened on Thu 1 Oct 2026 with judging quorum and took up >=1 case for discussion/voting — not off Turma sessions, not administrative/solemn sessions, not the virtual plenary, not monocratic decisions, not a session held only to read a decision or hear oral argument.
EVENT WINDOW: a single calendar day, Thu 2026-10-01 (Brasilia time) -> ends 2026-10-02T00:00Z per the criteria; as of Now (2026-09-21T10:10Z) 0% elapsed, ~10 days before it opens.
STATUS QUO OUTCOME: the STF plenary sits on its calendared Wednesdays and Thursdays and judges cases; cancellation requires an affirmative act by the presidency or absent justices.
EVIDENCE:
- STF 2026 judicial-year opening: plenary judgment sessions run on Wednesdays and Thursdays, resuming Wed 4 Feb 2026 (Migalhas, Feb 2026).
- Sept 2026 published plenary agenda listed in-person session blocks on Sept 2-3, 9-10, 16-17, 23-24 and Sept 30 (ConJur reproduction of the STF September pauta, 29 Aug 2026). The monthly agenda article stops at 30 Sept; Oct 1 would fall under the separate October agenda.
- October 2026 agenda highlights published by the STF list cases for 8 Oct (ADI 6553 Ferrograo; RE 1177984 right to silence), and later dates reported as 16 Oct (ADIs 5553/7755, ICMS agrotoxicos), 22 Oct (RE 1355228; ADI 7419) and 23 Oct (RE 1133118 nepotism; ADO 55 IGF), plus ADI 7524 in the month's last session. No case is reported for 1 Oct in any coverage retrieved; several other Wed/Thu dates (7, 14, 15, 21, 28, 29) likewise get no mention, so the highlights are selective, not a full calendar. Direct access to portal.stf.jus.br/pauta returned a TLS failure and noticias.stf.jus.br returned HTTP 403 — the primary calendar could not be read this run.
- Cancellations in Sept 2026, all crisis-driven: Wed 9 and Thu 10 Sept cancelled (ConJur 10/9, O Tempo, EM); Thu 17 Sept cancelled shortly after a public clash among Gilmar Mendes, Mendonca and Fux, motive not stated (DGABC 17/9); the Wed 23 Sept session, set to take up the Mendonca matter, was pulled from the agenda (Diario do Poder; O Brasilianista 18/9).
- Sessions held during the same crisis: extraordinary plenary Tue 15 Sept on the Moraes question of order, suspended by Flavio Dino's pedido de vista (up to 90 days); ordinary plenary Wed 16 Sept resumed the regular docket with an ITBI immunity case (Imirante 16/9; Times Brasil).
- As of 18 Sept reporting, the remaining in-person plenary days in September were 24 and 30, with the 24th set for ICMS tax-benefit ADIs and MP compensation (ADPF 557) and the 30th for ADPFs 618/642 on blood transfusions (O Brasilianista, 18 Sept 2026), which also wrote that it is not possible to predict whether September's calendared agendas will be judged on the scheduled dates.
- Reported presidential strategy: Fachin is slowing public treatment of the Moraes/Banco Master matters, keeping some cases with the presidency, and is evaluating leaving the minister-related analyses until after the elections — one account says after the second round (CNN Brasil blog, Gustavo Uribe; Blog do BG 20/9). A faction holds there is no environment to resume that judgment before voters go to the polls.
- Open triggers that could reignite the dispute before 1 Oct: Fachin must still decide on the suspension of PF director Andrei Rodrigues and on resuming the Master and INSS inquiries; an unresolved question of order on whether the president-rapporteur may cast a tie-breaking vote with the plenary split 4-4 (G1, 20 Sept 2026).
- Quorum mechanics: reporting says a plenary judgment session needs at least seven justices present (the court has 11); outlets reported some justices weighing staying away, which could obstruct the agenda. No justice has publicly committed to doing so.
- Calendar context: 1 Oct 2026 is a Thursday; first-round general elections are Sun 4 Oct; candidates have pre-election arrest immunity 19 Sept-6 Oct. No national or judiciary holiday falls on 1 Oct and the STF is not in recess (recesses are Jul 2-31 and Dec 20-Jan 31). Three STF justices also sit on the TSE, which is in its final pre-election stretch that week.
- Markets: no prediction-market contract on STF session activity was found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold; Brazil blocked 27 prediction-market platforms including Polymarket and Kalshi in April 2026. One adjacent Polymarket contract exists on impeachment/removal of an STF justice before 2027 — different event, different horizon.
BASE RATES FOUND: (a) over all calendared STF ordinary Wed/Thu plenary days in a normal term, sessions convene and judge nearly always — no published dataset found this run; derived from the calendar structure and routine 'Confira a pauta do STF desta quarta/quinta' daily notices. (b) over calendared plenary days in the Sept 2026 crisis window specifically (9, 10, 16, 17, 23 Sept): one of five held, the rest cancelled by the presidency. (c) over all Sept 2026 calendared days including the pre-crisis block (2, 3, 9, 10, 16, 17, 23): three of seven held, with 24 and 30 still pending as of Now. (d) no source found giving a historical rate of STF plenary sessions being held or skipped in the week before a first-round election; searches for STF plenary activity in late Sept 2022 and early Oct 2024 returned nothing usable.
SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: the actual STF pauta entry (or its absence) for 1 Oct 2026; any announcement suspending or emptying plenary sessions for election week; any statement by Fachin about the 30 Sept / 1 Oct block; confirmation of whether the 16 Oct / 23 Oct dates in the October highlights are accurate given the Wed/Thu rule (both are Fridays), which leaves the reported October date pattern unverified.
calls.reference_class: Scheduled STF ordinary Wednesday/Thursday in-person plenary session days (2024-2026) that actually convene with quorum and take up at least one case

calls.reasoning: Reference class: scheduled ordinary Thursday in-person STF plenary judgment sessions in non-recess weeks — these are held and take up at least one case roughly 90% of the time. Two adjustments pull down. (1) Regime: in the current Master-case crisis the STF cancelled 3 of ~6 scheduled ordinary plenary sessions in September 2026 (9, 10 and 17 Sep), two of them Thursdays, and ministers are reported to be weighing absences that would break quorum, with judgments expected to migrate to the virtual plenary, which does not count. (2) 1 Oct is three days before the 4 Oct first round, with 2-3 justices on TSE duty and some reluctance to act on charged matters. Offsetting: Thursday is a regimental session day, the court has already scheduled a substantive case for Wed 30 Sep, so election week is a working week; the 16 Sep ordinary session ran normally once crisis items were off the pauta; and Fachin's stated concern is precisely that his judgment agenda not be obstructed. The October pauta is not yet public, so scheduling is inferred, not confirmed. Crisis-regime weighting: ~55% chance sessions are running near-normally by then (~0.90 hit rate) and ~45% chance still disrupted (~0.55), times a modest election-week discount.
calls.dossier:
EVENT WINDOW: a single day — Thursday 1 Oct 2026, Brasilia local time (UTC-3), i.e. 2026-10-01T03:00Z to 2026-10-02T03:00Z per the criteria. As of Now (2026-09-21T10:10Z) 0% elapsed; the window opens in ~10 days.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off reporting about whether an IN-PERSON (presencial) plenary judgment session convened with judging quorum and took up >=1 case for discussion or voting. It does NOT resolve off virtual/electronic plenary sessions (the STF runs continuous multi-day virtual sessions, e.g. 18-25 Sep and 25 Sep-2 Oct 2026 windows, which overlap 1 Oct but do not count), nor Turma panel sessions, administrative or solemn sessions, oral-argument-only sittings, or monocratic decisions.

STRUCTURE / STATUS QUO: STF ordinary plenary sessions are held Wednesdays and Thursdays (afternoon, ~14h). 1 Oct 2026 is a Thursday, in term (STF recesses are 19 Dec-31 Jan and 2-31 Jul), not a Brazilian or Brasilia holiday. The published September 2026 plenary agenda (Conjur, 29 Aug 2026) lists Wed+Thu pairs every week: 2-3, 9-10, 16-17, 23-24, plus Wed 30 Sep (blood-transfusion ADPFs 618/642; psychology-council norms). O Brasilianista (18 Sep 2026) states the remaining in-person sessions of September are 24 and 30 Sep, and that it 'is not possible to predict if the agendas scheduled for September will still be judged on the predicted dates'.

OCTOBER AGENDA: as of 21 Sep 2026 I could not locate a published October 2026 plenary agenda. Search engines return the STF's October 2025 highlights article (Ferrograo ADI 6553, nepotism RE 1133118, wealth tax; session days 8/16/22/23 — weekday pattern matches 2025, not 2026). Searched for, not found: any STF notice confirming or cancelling a 1 Oct 2026 session; any STF notice about sessions during the election period; the STF official 2026 calendar PDF and the portal's pauta calendar were unreachable (403 / TLS errors) from this run.

SEPTEMBER 2026 SESSION RECORD (the relevant regime data):
- Week of 2-3 Sep: sessions on the published agenda (Funrural ADI 4.395, PIS/Cofins RE 1.479.774, ITBI RE 1.495.108, ADC 80, ADI 5.982); no report of cancellation found.
- Week of 9-10 Sep: BOTH plenary sessions cancelled by President Fachin amid the war of injunctions over the Federal Police director-general (O Tempo, 16 Sep; Agencia Brasil).
- Tue 15 Sep: extraordinary plenary session held on a question of order in Pet 16.662 (PF report on Moraes/Vorcaro messages); suspended by Flavio Dino's pedido de vista (up to 90 days). Vote count reported 4-4, with a dispute over whether the president-rapporteur may cast a tie-breaking vote (G1, 20 Sep).
- Wed 16 Sep: ordinary session HELD, opened ~14h50, judged ITBI immunity and other listed cases; Moraes and Mendonca both present; no mention of the crisis at the opening (n1n, 16 Sep).
- Thu 17 Sep: session CANCELLED by Fachin to contain escalation (Diario do Grande ABC, CNN Brasil, Agencia Brasil).
- Wed 23 Sep: the Mendonca matter (Pet 16.704) was withdrawn from the agenda on 17 Sep; ordinary items (ADI 7.935, ADPF 557, ICMS/SP ADIs) remained listed; status of the sitting itself unresolved as of 21 Sep.
Tally over scheduled ordinary sessions 2-17 Sep: 3 held (2, 3, 16 — the first two inferred from the agenda with no cancellation reported), 3 cancelled (9, 10, 17). Of the Thursdays 3, 10, 17: two cancelled.

BASE RATES:
- Over all scheduled ordinary Wednesday/Thursday in-person plenary sessions in non-recess weeks in normal periods (2024-2026): the large majority convene and judge at least one case; cancellations are occasional and driven by holidays, ceremonies, presidential travel, or an exhausted docket. I found no published count; this is an estimate from the regularity of the published monthly agendas, not a measured series.
- Over scheduled ordinary sessions GIVEN the September 2026 crisis regime: 3 of 6 held, per the record above (sources: O Tempo 16 Sep; Diario do Grande ABC 17 Sep; n1n 16 Sep).
- Over election weeks: I searched for, and did not find, any rule or precedent of the STF suspending plenary sessions in the week before a first-round election, nor a confirmed record of whether sessions were held on 28-29 Sep 2022 (before the 2 Oct 2022 first round); the STF Informativo editions covering that week exist (nos. 1068-1069) but were unreachable.

EVIDENCE POINTING ONE WAY (continuity): Thursday is a regimental session day; a substantive case is already scheduled for Wed 30 Sep, so election week is being treated as a working week; the 16 Sep ordinary session ran normally with full attendance once crisis items were off the agenda; Fachin is reported to be concerned that his judgment agenda (pejotizacao, uberizacao and other broad cases) could be obstructed, giving him an incentive to keep ordinary sittings running; the resolution bar is low (any one case taken up for discussion or voting).

EVIDENCE POINTING THE OTHER WAY (disruption): three cancellations in the three weeks to 21 Sep, two of them Thursdays; O Tempo (16 Sep) reports ministers expect coming sessions to be 'contaminated', that the president has contemplated sessions without quorum, and that ministers from rival blocs project a migration of judgments to the virtual plenary precisely to avoid in-person confrontation; the regimento's minimum presence is reported as six ministers in O Tempo and as seven in the question background, and constitutional-control judgments require eight; Brasil 247 (21 Sep) reports Fachin has decided to slow public plenary handling, keep the Master and INSS matters under his own hand, and 'buy time' via one-on-one meetings rather than convening the full court; unresolved flashpoints remain (Fachin's pending decision on the suspension of PF director Andrei Rodrigues, resumption of the Master and INSS inquiries, the contested tie-break rule); the first round is 4 Oct, 2-3 justices sit on the TSE which sits near-daily in the final election week, and justices had signalled reluctance to have the court act on politically
calls.reference_class: Scheduled ordinary Thursday in-person STF plenary judgment sessions in non-recess weeks (2024-2026), of which ~90% convene with quorum and take up at least one case; conditional on the September 2026 crisis regime the realized rate was 3 of 6 scheduled sessions held.

calls.reasoning: Scheduled ordinary Thursday in-person STF plenary sittings convene and judge at least one case ~90% of the time; two discounts apply. Scheduling gate ~0.88: the Oct 2026 pauta is unpublished/unreachable, but September ran Wed+Thu every week and 30 Sep is already pauta'd with substantive ADPFs, so election week is a working week. Run 2's claim that the October agenda lists only Oct 8 onward is a retrieval of the October 2025 article (Oct 16/23 are Fridays in 2026, Thursdays in 2025), so it carries no weight against Oct 1. Conditional hold ~0.80: Fachin cancelled 9, 10, 17 and 23 Sep amid the Master-case crisis (only 16 Sep held in that window), but the flashpoints are now parked — Dino's vista runs up to 90 days, the Mendonca matter is off-calendar, and minister matters are reported deferred past the vote — which is exactly the condition under which 16 Sep ran normally on the ordinary tax/rights docket. The quorum-break story is overweighted by all three runs: the RISTF floor is six (eight only for constitutional-control merits), so the live NO channel is discretionary presidential cancellation plus migration to the 25 Sep-2 Oct virtual session, which does not count. 0.88 x 0.80 = 0.70.
calls.reconciliation: No web access this run; reconciled on the dossiers. Settled two factual disputes. (1) Run 2's 'October 2026 agenda' listing Oct 8/16/22/23 is the October 2025 highlights page — the weekday pattern only fits 2025 (Oct 1 2025 = Wednesday), and in 2026 Oct 16 and 23 are Fridays, incompatible with the Wed/Thu rule; Run 2 noticed the inconsistency but did not resolve it. Its 'Oct 1 not on the pauta' discount is therefore void, which lifts my scheduling gate above Run 1's 0.85. (2) The 23 Sep in-person session: Runs 1 and 2 carry O Brasilianista (18 Sep, corroborated by Diario do Poder/Noveen) saying the remaining September in-person days are 24 and 30, so the sitting was cancelled, not merely stripped of the Mendonca item; the crisis-window record is thus 1 of 5 held, worse than Run 3's 3-of-6, which offsets the gain from (1). Unsettled: whether the plenary floor is six (RISTF per O Tempo) or seven (question background) — left carrying its uncertainty, but it barely moves the number, since either way a quorum break needs 5+ absences and the realistic NO path is discretionary cancellation. Pure judgment, no evidence breaking the tie: whether the crisis regime still suppresses in-person sittings on 1 Oct. I bet on continuity — the acute triggers are parked past the election and Fachin's stated concern is that his own judgment agenda not be obstructed — but only at ~60/40. I adopted Run 3's reference class and base rate (~0.90) and rebuilt the discounts myself rather than averaging; landing at 0.70 is my decomposition's output, not a split of the runs.

disagreements.claim: The October 2026 STF agenda was published and names cases only from Oct 8 onward, implying Oct 1 may not be scheduled
disagreements.verdict: Refuted — the retrieved article is the October 2025 highlights; Oct 16/23 are Fridays in 2026 but Thursdays in 2025, and the whole date set fits 2025's Wed/Thu pattern exactly. No evidence exists either way on Oct 1's scheduling, so the discount is removed.

disagreements.claim: The Wed 23 Sep plenary session was cancelled outright, versus only the Mendonca item being pulled from it
disagreements.verdict: Settled as cancelled — O Brasilianista (18 Sep), Diario do Poder and Noveen all report the remaining September in-person plenary days as 24 and 30 only. Crisis-window hold rate is therefore 1 of 5, not 3 of 6.

disagreements.claim: A plenary judgment session requires at least six justices present (RISTF) or at least seven (question background)
disagreements.verdict: Could not be settled without the RISTF text; left uncertain. Immaterial to the number — under either floor a quorum break needs five or more absences, and the 16 Sep session convened with the contested justices present, so cancellation by the presidency, not quorum failure, is the operative NO channel.

disagreements.claim: The crisis regime that produced four September cancellations will still be suppressing in-person plenary sittings on 1 Oct
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks it. Weighted ~40% still-disrupted against ~60% near-normal, on the grounds that the Moraes vista (up to 90 days) and the off-calendar Mendonca matter remove the items that triggered every crisis cancellation, and 30 Sep is pauta'd with substantive cases.

disagreements.claim: Election-week proximity (first round 4 Oct, three justices on TSE duty) independently suppresses the 1 Oct session
disagreements.verdict: Downweighted. All three runs searched for a rule or precedent of the STF clearing plenary sessions before a first round and none found one; the already-scheduled 30 Sep substantive session is direct evidence the court treats that week as a working week. Retained only as a small discount inside the disrupted branch.

disagreements.claim: A prediction market prices this event
disagreements.verdict: No. All three runs found nothing on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold; the harness's Polymarket candidate is an STF-justice-impeachment-before-2027 contract (0.04, $92k volume) — different event, deadline and resolution source. Treated as evidence, not an anchor.
